Subject: Explore Optimize pilot — credits / quantization guidance needed

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the Optimize toolkit looks promising for reducing our per-token costs on high-throughput customer messages. Before we can move to a pilot I need two things from Redwood:

- A pilot economics proposal (what credits / discounts do you typically offer for a 6-week pilot with ~50k tokens/day baseline)
- High-level recommendations on quantization and batching for our workload (95th pct latency target 150ms, bursts to 300 qps)

Attached is our security questionnaire and a sample throughput CSV. We’d like to run an initial integration in our staging VPC — is that possible under a pilot?

Sara Jenkins
Head of Platform
Opsly

Hi Sara — great to meet you yesterday. Appreciate the throughput profile. Quick answers up-front; details below and I’ve looped in Monica (commercial lead) and Rishi (inference engineering) for the pilot ops.

Pilot economics (6 weeks) — typical structure we propose:
- $0 setup fee; pilot credits equal to 25% of expected 6-week consumption (we can set explicit caps).
- Optional 2-week extension if integration spikes — requires quick commercial approval.

Quantization & batching guidance (initial recommendation):
- Start with int8 quantization for the large LLM variant (best balance of throughput & quality).
- Use dynamic batching with a max batch latency budget of 60ms and per-request tail-latency SLOs. That should keep 95th under 150ms for your baseline; we’ll tune for burst behavior.
- Enable prefix KV caching on conversation roots to save ~15-25% tokens depending on reuse.

Staging VPC access: yes, we can do a private deployment slice for the pilot; we’ll provide a short checklist for your infra team.

I’ve attached a quick cost model that shows the credit math for 25/50/100k tokens/day. Monica — can you propose the exact credit amount and any required paperwork? Rishi — can you confirm the runtime settings below are ok and whether we should recommend int4 for aggressive cost savings?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

- Commercial: We can approve a simple pilot credit of $12,500 (covers ~25% of 6-week estimated consumption at 50k tokens/day). Include one 2-week extension option. No upfront commit.
- Legal/Procurement: Opsly’s request for staging VPC access will require an MSA addendum; attach their security questionnaire (I’ll kick to Legal).

Rishi, pricing question: can runtime support int8 by default and offer int4 as a config flag? Opsly cares about cost but also latency. If int4 degrades 95th pct by >20ms we should avoid unless customer is comfortable.

Rishi: can you provide a 2-paragraph blurb we can share with Opsly explaining the tradeoffs (latency, quality delta, fallback)? Keep it non-technical for procurement.

Monica

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & technical credit breakdown — Optimize toolkit

Monica / Dylan — here’s the blurb and a couple of tuning notes you can forward to Opsly.

Blurb for procurement (non-technical):
Redwood Optimize recommends int8 quantization for production pilots — it typically reduces GPU compute cost by ~40% with negligible perceptible quality change for customer-facing text generation. For customers with extremely tight cost targets, int4 is an advanced option but may require additional evaluation; we enable automatic fallback to int8 if quality regressions are detected.

Tuning notes for engineering (short):
- Runtime config: int8 + dynamic batching (max batch latency 60ms) + prefix KV caching enabled.
- If Opsly wants to test int4, run A/B with 10% of traffic for 1 week and monitor perplexity/semantic drift on a validation prompt set; expect 5–12% further compute savings but potential 5–10% QA delta depending on model.

I also attached a brief security note about VPC peering requirements and a sample pilot runbook we use for staging slices. Happy to walk Opsly’s infra team through a 30-min tech sync.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference
